item.title: 0.6.0-beta.7
item.description:
# Agent HUD 0.6.0-beta.7
## Compatibility
**Requires Agent HUD for iPhone 1.7.2 or later** for iPhone and Apple Watch sync. Update the iPhone app before updating the Mac. Older iPhone versions cannot read this release's data.
[Get the iPhone app](https://apps.apple.com/app/id6812113619).
If the required iPhone version is not yet on the App Store, cross-device features require the corresponding TestFlight version.
Requires an Apple Silicon Mac running macOS 14 or later.
## Changes
### Coming from 0.5.5
- Includes everything in [0.6.0-beta.1](https://github.com/jazzenchen/agent-hud-open/releases/tag/v0.6.0-beta.1), which moves Agent HUD to a new cross-platform app and brings your settings and 30 days of quota history with it, and the changes in [0.6.0-beta.2](https://github.com/jazzenchen/agent-hud-open/releases/tag/v0.6.0-beta.2), [0.6.0-beta.3](https://github.com/jazzenchen/agent-hud-open/releases/tag/v0.6.0-beta.3), [0.6.0-beta.4](https://github.com/jazzenchen/agent-hud-open/releases/tag/v0.6.0-beta.4), [0.6.0-beta.5](https://github.com/jazzenchen/agent-hud-open/releases/tag/v0.6.0-beta.5) and [0.6.0-beta.6](https://github.com/jazzenchen/agent-hud-open/releases/tag/v0.6.0-beta.6).
### New
- Lets an agent build the hover panel through the HUD tools, not only rearrange it: - Controls of its own: rows, columns, grids, text, logos, bars, rings, segments, the token chart, dividers and pickers, in the panel's own fonts and colours in both looks, among the agents' blocks or as sections of their own. A list can repeat for each window, balance, account, agent or session, with figures and reset times written as the panel's rows write them, and a clock that turns with the minute. A click opens Statistics, a session or a Settings page, or copies text. - The panel's sections side by side: Quota details, Token usage and the Session list can share a row as columns, and the panel can be 480 to 960 points wide (up to 720 before). - Compact quota blocks: a block drawn as rings or segments can drop its list of windows and become a square tile with the logo, name and plan, the measure picker, one ring with the most used window's figure, and when that window resets. Up to six tiles share a line. Pointing at the ring shows each window. - Offers Reply rate, Consumed and Est. cost for more agents than Claude and Codex, wherever Agent HUD logs the calls that spend a window: - Antigravity, Cursor, Copilot, Devin, Factory Droid, Grok Bot, Grok CLI, Qoder, WorkBuddy, Cline and Hermes's Nous Portal credits; Kimi's, GLM's, OpenCode Go's and MiniMax's plans, Claude Code's calls with the plan's key included; and Pi's calls with its ChatGPT sign-in, in that account's Codex windows. - Claude's all-models windows count only Claude models, and a call through a relay or a local model server no longer counts toward its client's own plan. - Every quota and balance block offers all its measures, and greys one only when its readings can't give it. A saved layout that limited the picker no longer does. - Tells you in the HUD when Codex skips Agent HUD's hooks until you allow them, and what is missing meanwhile: its approvals, or only its sessions' progress. Codex runs them once you click Review hooks above its message box, then Allow all. On macOS the notice's button brings Codex forward or opens it. The notice comes 20 seconds after launch, then at most once a day. - Answers Copilot CLI's permission requests in the HUD once you turn on Settings → Agents → Copilot → Answer permission requests in the HUD. It is off by default and works while client hooks are on. Every tool call Copilot would run or ask about then waits for your answer in the HUD; runs started with `-p`, `--allow-all-tools`, `--allow-all` or `--yolo` stay with Copilot. - Draws the sub-agent timeline on a session's page more calmly: calls close together join one run instead of a row of ticks, and split again as you zoom in. A sideways trackpad swipe, or Shift with a mouse wheel, pans a zoomed view, and zooming and panning glide instead of jumping. - Shows TRAE and TRAE CN with TRAE's own logo instead of a generic icon, and each agent's logo in Settings → Display → Panel → Agent order. - Installs from a terminal: `brew install --cask jazzenchen/tap/agent-hud` on a Mac, or `npx @agenthud/install` on a Mac, Windows or Linux. Both install the newest release, betas included. The npx installer checks the download against the release's checksums, and on a Mac also Agent HUD's signature. If Agent HUD is already in Applications, add `--adopt` to the Homebrew command.
### Fixes
- Orders the HUD's marks by the agent order in Settings also after an agent chose through the HUD tools which marks show. The marks kept the agent's order, so reordering in Settings moved only the panel's blocks. The menu bar's agents follow the same order. - Lets the HUD tools change a panel whose saved layout keeps a setting from a block's earlier look, such as columns on a rings block. Every edit to such a panel was refused. - Takes the HUD tools' picture of the panel on a busy Mac: after 8 seconds of waiting for the token chart and the session list, it takes the picture and says what had not loaded, instead of timing out. A picture that still times out says which step it was waiting for. - Stops adding a second, stale Claude account when Claude Code is signed out and the Claude desktop app is signed in to another account. Claude Code's usage record now stands in only for the account it belongs to. - Follows some agents more closely: - Devin: one card for each Devin request. Devin also runs Claude Code's hooks, so a request could reach the HUD a second time as a Claude Code session. A session in Devin Desktop's terminal names Devin, not Windsurf, as where its messages were typed. Not yet checked with an installed Devin. - Factory Droid: a command that Droid's own settings already allow or block no longer waits in the HUD; Droid decides it alone. A command an ask rule names waits for your answer at every autonomy level, High included. Read from Factory's docs and not yet checked with a running Droid. - Hermes: its hooks go into every Hermes profile that is set up, not only the default one, so a profile's sessions show live, each under its profile. Hermes asks once in each profile to allow them. - Hermes: when its Nous Portal sign-in has expired, the last credits stay, then show as stale with a note that they update the next time Hermes runs. It showed a failure at once. - Qoder and Qoder CN: their hooks go to the folder `QODER_CONFIG_DIR` or `QODERCN_CONFIG_DIR` names, where Qoder keeps its settings, instead of always `~/.qoder` and `~/.qoder-cn`. - MiniMax and Volcengine Ark: their plans are read every five minutes, also while no agent works on this computer. Other apps and devices spend them too, so a reading could stay hours behind. - Keeps the Simple dock's background and outline while its usage panel is open. A panel shorter than the dock left the dock's ends bare, its bots drawn over whatever was behind. - Keeps the Settings window still when a trackpad scroll runs past its end. macOS sometimes left the page drawn about 20 points higher, with the sidebar taking clicks one row from where it was drawn. - Shows a page that fails to draw in Settings or Statistics as an error under the page's header, with the sidebar still there, instead of a blank window.

# Agent HUD 0.5.5
## Compatibility
**Requires Agent HUD for iPhone 1.5 or later** for iPhone and Apple Watch sync. Update the iPhone app before updating the Mac. Older iPhone versions cannot read this release's data.
[Get the iPhone app](https://apps.apple.com/app/id6812113619).
Requires an Apple Silicon Mac running macOS 14 or later.
## Changes
### Quota names on every device
- Keeps quota window names and short forms in English, so an English iPhone, widget or Apple Watch no longer receives Chinese names from a Mac using Chinese. Names update after the Mac reads and syncs the account again.
### Docks and appearance
- Keeps every logo visible on Simple and Dynamic docks while a reply or request opens beside the sending agent's logo. - Gives each display its own dark, light or system appearance, solid or glass material and transparency. Settings → General can match windows to their display's HUD as an experimental option. - Lets both dock sizes run from 20 to 60 pt, adds Simple panel logo spacing and uses one smaller text size for dock numbers, reminders and the hover line. - Makes the agents' bots act out thinking, tools, approvals, questions, plans, compaction, failures and usage limits. Claude's bot is Clawd. - Keeps the menu bar's figure, colours and agent order in step with the main display's HUD and its layout.
### Arrange the HUD with an agent
- Adds client checkmarks and add/remove actions for the MCP server in Settings → Experimental. - Names the tools `get_hud`, `get_hud_screenshot`, `draft_hud`, `discard_hud_draft` and `finish_hud_edit`. The server remains `agent-hud`; turn on the renamed HUD tools switch again to use it. - Lets an agent filter sessions by project and period, choose block accounts and row order, change panel switches and propose app settings as a draft for you to save. - Holds the panel open while an agent arranges it, then lets go when the edit finishes or you dismiss it. - Adds balance burn rates, estimated run-out times and cost charts to API balance blocks.
### Sessions and other agents
- Removes archived or deleted sessions from session lists while keeping their tokens in the usage totals until the ledger expires them. - Lets a session using a tool take over an agent's mark from one that is thinking. - Answers Claude Code plan approvals on the HUD, including accepting edits or returning feedback to keep planning. - Ends Claude Code turns promptly when their logs report a usage limit or API failure. - Keeps one provider order across Settings, the HUD, glow, menu bar and token statistics. - Shows WorkBuddy's model ceilings and credits, reads a GLM plan held only by WorkBuddy under that group and handles a CodeBuddy CLI using WorkBuddy's configuration as WorkBuddy. - Reduces artwork memory, repeated island layout and process inspection for clients that are not installed.
### iPhone and Apple Watch sync
- Sends Claude's narrations and questions to the phone, including questions answered through the Claude desktop app's next-step box. - Keeps published turn text once and improves local-network change tracking and conversation-cache recovery. - Ships the Mac executable stripped and the updater for Apple Silicon only, while keeping debugging symbols locally for crash reports.
